# Installed release APK startup failure
Investigated: 13 November 2026.
## Confirmed cause
The connected Xiaomi phone (model reported by ADB: M2101K7BNY, Android 13) recorded this startup failure for the installed production package:
`java.lang.IllegalAccessError: Class kotlin.text.j extended by class sz2 is inaccessible`
The exported release mapping identifies `kotlin.text.j` as `kotlin.text.StringsKt__IndentKt` and `sz2` as `kotlin.text.StringsKt__StringBuilderKt`. Release optimization repackaged the subclass outside the inaccessible parent's package. The failure occurs during Kotlin reflection initialization on activity startup, before login.
This explains why the non-optimized Android Studio debug build starts while the previously exported release APK crashes. This exception is not evidence of a missing permission, an authentication role failure, or a phone hardware fault.
## Fix
`app/build.gradle.kts` explicitly disables release code optimization. Do not restore the previous `androidx.**` / `kotlin.**` / `kotlinx.**` scoped optimization until an optimizer update or narrower workaround passes installed-release tests. The resulting release APK is larger; the build remains non-debuggable. No signing credentials, authentication policy, or stored user data were changed.
## Build and installation
- Rebuild using Android Studio's **Generate Signed App Bundle / APK** action, selecting **APK**, **release**, and the existing release key. - Install the newly generated signed APK as an update. Do not uninstall the existing production app to work around signing errors: uninstalling removes app data and device enrollment. - The previously exported `app/release/app-release.apk` is not automatically replaced by a command-line unsigned release build. Do not reuse the old export. - Command-line `assembleRelease` without a configured signing key produces an unsigned APK, not a distributable signed update. Keep key passwords out of source control, terminal logs, and chat.
## Local verification records
Release and non-debuggable smoke APK builds passed. All 87 JVM tests passed with zero failures/errors. Release lint reported zero errors, 50 warnings, and two hints. The unsigned fixed release is `app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release-unsigned.apk` (17,454,041 bytes).
Device startup validation remains **blocked**: MIUI rejected the separate test APK with `INSTALL_FAILED_USER_RESTRICTED: Install canceled by user`. No cold launches ran and no UI hierarchy was captured. USB installation must be allowed by the device owner before retrying. The existing production package remained installed and unchanged.
Build/JVM test/release lint output: `app/build/release-startup-verification.log`. Original crash: `app/build/release-startup-original-crash.txt`. Phone smoke-test output: `app/build/release-startup-phone-validation.txt`.
The local validation init script `app/build/notes-release-smoke.init.gradle` creates a non-debuggable variant inheriting the release configuration with a separate `.releasesmoke` application ID and the debug signing key. It is for startup testing only, not distribution. The test removes only that separate package afterward; it does not replace the installed production app.
Startup smoke testing does not validate live backend operations, biometric sign-in, the final production signature, or every supported Android version. The connected model above is not a Redmi Note 8; a Note 8-specific result must be recorded separately if that is a different target device.
